Transition triggers (Step 0-3): the "Cyclical → Quality" trigger requires ROIC > WACC
across 3 consecutive cycles with reduced margin volatility. VIK has only 4 fiscal years
of data and one post-IPO credit cycle. **~60% of the transition criteria are met**
(returns yes, cycle-testing no). Therefore: **Blended Engine.**

**0-2. Valuation engine selected (my selection, not pre-set)**

**Engine 1 (DCF on Adjusted EBITDA → FCFF) × 60%**
**Engine 2 (Cycle-adjusted / normalized owner-earnings multiple) × 25%**
**Engine 3 (Hybrid: attach-revenue / installed-base contribution) × 15%**

Engine 3 is NOT applied as a "platform premium" multiplier. Per Rule 7, a platform
premium requires numerical backing; Viking's only platform-like asset is its repeat-guest
base and attach revenue (~40% of guests purchase pre/post-voyage land extensions —
[Actual], Q2 2026 call). I therefore model attach revenue **as a revenue line inside
the Engine 1 forecast** and use Engine 3 only as a qualitative cross-check. It receives
no separate valuation premium.

**0-3. Why not another engine**

| Alternative | Error it would cause |
|---|---|
| Engine 4 (Expectation-Driven) | VIK has $6.5B revenue, +$2.0B adj EBITDA, positive FCF. Treating it as option-value would overstate value by ignoring that the cash flows already exist. |
| Engine 5 (Probability-Weighted Binary) | No single regulatory gate. Wrong tool. |
| Engine 1 only | Rules 1 and 2 forbid a DCF-only conclusion. Requires the Engine 2 cross-check. |
| Engine 2 only (Peak/Trough) | Would imply capacity and bookings are noise. They are contracted. Wrong. |
